sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Anderson County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
A deed for land in Anderson County goes to the Anderson County Clerk, whose office is at 100 S Main St in Lawrenceburg, KY 40342. Kentucky law sends every deed to the clerk of the county where the land lies, or where most of it lies if the parcel crosses a line (KRS 382.110).

The clerk's Legal Records Department keeps the deed, mortgage, lien, will and marriage books. Lawrenceburg is the county seat and the largest city, and Anderson County was carved out of Franklin, Washington and Mercer counties in 1827. A seller here records nothing personally in most sales. The closing attorney or title agent carries the signed deed to the clerk, collects the fees and transfer tax at the counter, and returns the stamped original later.

sections.h2: What is the Anderson County housing market like for a seller?
sections.html:
Anderson County is a growing Outer Bluegrass county of about 25,225 people (Census estimate for July 2025), up from 23,852 at the 2020 count. It borders Franklin, Woodford, Mercer, Washington, Nelson, Spencer and Shelby counties and sits inside the Frankfort micropolitan area, so many owners commute out of the county.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $225,100 (2020 to 2024 Census survey).
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.6 percent, with 9,653 households and 10,652 housing units.
  • Median household income: $74,488, with a mean commute of 30.4 minutes.
  • Median gross rent: $927 a month.

A high owner-occupancy rate and a long commute fit a county where most sales are ordinary family-home transfers, and the paperwork below is mostly routine.

sections.h2: What must a deed say before the Anderson County Clerk will accept it?
sections.html:
The clerk may not file a deed that leaves out the items in KRS 382.135, and the same office can refuse a deed that skips the title source in KRS 382.110. Check the draft against this list before closing day.

  • The full names and mailing addresses of grantor and grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An in-care-of address where the current year's property tax bill can be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the price in the deed is the full price paid. A gift deed instead states that it is a gift and gives the estimated fair cash value.
  • The immediate source of the grantor's title, with office, book, page and recording date. If the owner inherited, the deed says how and from whom.

A property that passed by will or intestacy needs one more filing. The estate's personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk listing who received each parcel and its value before the estate closes.

sections.h2: How much does the Anderson County Clerk charge to record?
sections.html:
The clerk posts a statewide minimum fee schedule that took effect January 1, 2020. A standard deed is $50. Documents over five pages cost $3 for every extra page, and mortgages add $3 per page past page thirty. KRS 142.010 separately puts a $4 state tax on each conveyance of real property, which the clerk collects and sends to the Department of Revenue, so ask the counter whether a quoted total already includes it.

Seller-side recording is usually one deed and one mortgage release, so the clerk's charges on a typical sale are a small part of closing costs.

sections.h2: How is the Kentucky transfer tax figured on an Anderson County sale?
sections.html:
The grantor pays fifty cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, declared in the deed (KRS 142.050). The clerk does the arithmetic and will not accept the deed until the tax is paid.

As an illustration only, a sale at $225,100 holds 450 full units of $500 plus a remainder, so it counts as 451 units and the tax comes to $225.50. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration, the value is the open-market price instead of the stated figure.

The clerk keeps five percent of the tax as a collection fee and sends the rest to the county treasurer every three months for the county general fund. Several transfers owe nothing:

  • Foreclosure transfers and deeds given in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds between spouses, or between former spouses in a divorce.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal consideration.
  • Deeds that only secure or release a debt, or correct an earlier recorded deed.
  • Transfers after a sale for delinquent taxes, and partitions.

The clerk's forms page offers an Exempt Transfer Affidavit (Form 71A245) for sellers who claim one of these.

sections.h2: How do you search Anderson County land records?
sections.html:
The clerk's records page says deeds and mortgages are indexed and scanned in the CCLIX system back to 1966, while wills and marriages reach back to 1797. Most instrument images from January 2004 to the present can be viewed online, and some older records go back to the 1700s on microfilm.

Online viewing runs through eCCLIX, which needs an account and password from the vendor, Software Management LLC, and charges access fees. Anyone can view the same public records free in the clerk's office. The clerk also offers DocAlert, a free email notice whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name. Homeowners who rent out property or live elsewhere use it as an early warning for deed fraud.

sections.h2: What happens in Anderson County when property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid bills leave the Sheriff's Office at the close of business on April 15 and become certificates of delinquency at the County Clerk. The Sheriff's tax page lists what is added there: a 20 percent County Attorney fee, a 10 percent Clerk fee and interest of 1 percent per month. The debt can be sold to a third party in the summer.

Under KRS 134.015, a recorded delinquency lien stays with the property whoever owns it, for up to eleven years. A buyer or title agent will find it, so a seller should expect the payoff to come out of the sale proceeds. The clerk's site has a delinquent-tax lookup, and the Sheriff's Office at 208 S Main St, (502) 839-4021, takes payment before April 15.

sections.h2: What should an Anderson County seller do before the deed is signed?
sections.html:
• Pull the vesting deed and note its book and page so the new deed can cite it.
  • Ask the Sheriff's Office for the current-year bill and any prior-year balance.
  • Ask the clerk for a payoff on any recorded lien, then plan the release recording.
  • Give the title agent a mailing address for the grantee's tax bill.
  • Decide whether any transfer-tax exemption applies and prepare the affidavit.

Sellers who want a faster path can ask for a written cash offer on the house as it stands, and the same deed and recording steps apply once a price is agreed.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a house in Lawrenceburg?
faqs.a: The Anderson County Clerk at 100 S Main St, Lawrenceburg, records it. The same county clerk handles property in every Anderson County town, because KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the clerk of the county where the land sits.

faqs.q: What does a deed cost to record in Anderson County?
faqs.a: The posted minimum is $50 for a deed, plus $3 for each page past five. KRS 142.010 adds a $4 state tax on a conveyance, so confirm the total with the clerk before sending a check.

faqs.q: Who pays the Kentucky transfer tax?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller, pays it. The rate is $0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction under KRS 142.050, and the clerk collects it when the deed is presented.

faqs.q: Can I view old Anderson County deeds without paying?
faqs.a: Yes, in person. The clerk's records page says every public record and index can be viewed free in the office. Online viewing through eCCLIX needs a paid account.

faqs.q: Does a deed in lieu of foreclosure owe transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. KRS 142.050 exempts transfers under a foreclosure proceeding and voluntary surrenders under a mortgage in lieu of foreclosure. The lender must file that deed with the county clerk within 45 days of signing under KRS 382.110.
